title: Drop the unused rayon pool and its facade from the susi binary
goal: Reduce the CPU work of the cold `cargo build -p susi` on Linux x86_64 without changing behaviour: the binary built a global rayon thread pool at startup and logged its size, but no crate in its build runs work on rayon (the GAWD crates moved to `susi_core::parallel` on 2026-11-07), so the pool, the `rayon` dependency and the `susi-vendor-rayon` facade go, and rayon, rayon-core, crossbeam-deque and crossbeam-epoch leave the build.

results.change: Root Cargo.toml: `rayon` dependency and the `crates/susi-vendor-rayon` member removed; the facade crate deleted. src/main.rs: the `ThreadPoolBuilder::build_global()` call and its log line removed (nothing ran on the pool). The `bloat-audit` help text said 'rayon-parallel'; it runs on std scoped threads (`susi_core::parallel::map_ref`), so it now says 'in parallel', with the CLI help snapshot updated. Cargo.lock drops only the facade entry: rayon stays locked as criterion's benchmark dev-dependency, but it is no longer in the `cargo build -p susi` graph (`cargo tree -p susi -e normal,build` lists no rayon, rayon-core, crossbeam-deque or crossbeam-epoch; crossbeam-utils and crossbeam-channel stay through tracing-appender).
results.measurement_method: Alternated fully cold `cargo build -p susi --offline --locked --timings` into empty target directories, base worktree at 4e49f290b then this change, two pairs back to back; load average and rustc count recorded before each run.

limitations: The saving is about 4 CPU-seconds and 12 units of a cold build; whole-build wall time is inside this host's load noise and is not claimed (the second pair's change run met rising load: unit CPU 338 s).

`tests/architecture_tests.rs` still lists `susi-vendor-rayon` in VENDOR_FACADES (a set lookup that does not require the crate to exist, like the unused `susi-vendor-flume` entry); that file is in another agent's scope, so the stale name is owed to its owner.

The GMCP `bloat_audit` tool description in `crates/susi-gmcp/src/tools/core.rs` still says 'rayon-parallel'; correcting it changes a pinned tool definition and needs a GMCP evidence re-record, so it is owed to the next GMCP landing.

provenance.agent: corecut (Cursor subagent, CachyOS Linux x86_64, CEO laptop)
